title: Etz Chaim (The Tree of Life)
author: Chaim Vital (Sefaria Community trans)
description: Etz Chaim (The Tree of Life) by Rabbi Chaim Vital (1543-1620), here in the community English translation from Sefaria. Vital was the chief disciple of Isaac Luria (the Ari) in sixteenth-century Safed, and Etz Chaim is the principal systematic presentation of Lurianic Kabbalah. Organised into 'palaces' and 'gates', it begins with the hall of Adam Kadmon and the round and direct lights, and describes tzimtzum (God's self-contraction to make space for creation), the line of light (kav), Adam Kadmon and the lights emanating from his eyes, ears, nose and mouth, the shattering of the vessels (shevirat ha-kelim), the partzufim or divine 'faces' (Arikh Anpin, Abba, Imma, Zeir Anpin and Nukva), the worlds of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah and Assiyah, and tikkun, the restoration of the world through human action. It is the foundation of all later Kabbalah and essential for the library's Adam Kadmon studies.
